pc_new: WAAS inspects north-south traffic at the app container, behind the ingress controller
quote: WAAS enhances the traditional WAF protection model by deploying closer to the application, easily scaling up or down, and allowing for inspection of "internal" traffic (east-to-west) from other microservices as well as inbound traffic (north-to-south).
notes: WAAS binds to the app container or host (deploy-waas) and the docs show an NGINX image scope example. No ingress controller connector is documented. The deployment-troubleshooting page tells users to set the ingress controller as a transparent proxy so WAAS sees client IPs, which confirms WAAS sits behind the ingress.
ak_onprem_note: docs/resources/deployment.md says the platform and policies stay the same in every model, and the on-prem control plane is Kubernetes native with an NGINX ingress gateway (docs/getting-started/on-prem-installation-guide.md). No API-security-specific on-prem page exists.

param: TLS vs Non-TLS Classification at Ingress
pc_new: WAAS inspects TLS per endpoint with a supplied certificate, but has no TLS vs non-TLS report
quote: A certificate (public certificate and private key files in PEM format) is required if the application employs TLS.
notes: WAAS in-line supports TLS 1.0 to 1.3 and out-of-band TLS 1.0 to 1.2 (waas-intro). The endpoint setup has a TLS on/off switch per endpoint. Neither the WAAS Monitor pages nor the analytics page list a view that classifies traffic as TLS or non-TLS.
ak_onprem_note: docs/faqs/api-sec.md lists TLS misconfiguration detection as an API security finding, and docs/resources/deployment.md says the platform is the same on premises.

pc_new: WAAS API discovery flags endpoints with credit card, PII and session data
quote: Endpoints with sensitive data such as Credit card, PII, ID query parameter, Session cookies, and so on.
notes: Sensitive data is defined by regex or location rules under Defend > WAAS > Sensitive data. The log-scrubbing page says the scanner samples mirrored traffic and does not inspect the request body field, so body coverage is partial.
ak_onprem_note: docs/resources/deployment.md says the platform is the same in every model. docs/use-cases/api-security.md has no on-prem caveat for the inventory view.

pc_new: WAAS alerts or blocks requests to paths missing from the imported API spec
quote: Request sent to a resource path that is not specified in the API resources list.
notes: The Enterprise-era cell cited an API endpoint inventory page that is not in the Compute docs. In Compute the capability is the Unspecified path(s)/method(s) action (Alert or Prevent) in API protection, plus API discovery that exports learned endpoints as OpenAPI 3.0. It works per request and raises audit events. No shadow API report or label is documented.
ak_onprem_note: docs/use-cases/api-security.md compares scans against an uploaded OpenAPI file in the control plane, and docs/resources/deployment.md says the platform is the same on premises.

pc_new: API discovery shows a last-seen date per endpoint, but no zombie API flag
quote: It shows information such as Path, HTTP method, Hits, API protection status, Path risks, Workload that’s running these resources, Image Risk factors, Resource Vulnerabilities, App ID, and last seen date.
notes: An admin can read the last-seen date and judge staleness by hand. The Console deletes older discovery entries by Last Observed date to save resources, which removes the history a zombie check would need. No comparison of spec against traffic for inactive endpoints is documented.
ak_onprem_note: docs/use-cases/api-security.md defines Zombie APIs as endpoints that are no longer active but still exist in the spec, and docs/resources/deployment.md says the platform is the same on premises.

pc_new: No DSPM. Compute Edition ships the CWPP module only
quote: Prisma Cloud Compute Edition is a self-hosted offering that’s deployed and managed by you. It includes the Cloud Workload Protection Platform (CWPP) module only.
notes: Enterprise Edition DSPM does not exist in Compute Edition. Nothing in Compute resembles stored-data discovery for S3 or databases. The nearest items are WAAS sensitive data rules on HTTP traffic and secrets checks inside images and containers (compliance/detect-secrets).
ak_onprem_note: docs/getting-started/dspm-overview.md runs the console on premises or air-gapped, but the self-managed scanner covers only PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, SQL Server and MongoDB. Self-managed object storage and SMB or NFS shares are not supported, and S3, Blob and Drive need cloud reach.

pc_new: No data classification. Compute Edition ships the CWPP module only
quote: Prisma Cloud Compute Edition is a self-hosted offering that’s deployed and managed by you. It includes the Cloud Workload Protection Platform (CWPP) module only.
notes: Compute has no classifier for stored data. WAAS lets admins write regex or location rules to mark sensitive data in HTTP traffic, and log scrubbing redacts it in logs. That is not data classification.
ak_onprem_note: docs/getting-started/dspm-overview.md says the scanner classifies in memory and the console can run on premises or air-gapped, so the 283 classes and country packs apply to the stores it can reach.

pc_new: No data access mapping. Compute Edition ships the CWPP module only
quote: Prisma Cloud Compute Edition is a self-hosted offering that’s deployed and managed by you. It includes the Cloud Workload Protection Platform (CWPP) module only.
notes: Enterprise Edition DSPM data asset access views have no Compute counterpart. The AccuKnox cell for this row is Coming soon, so it is not a differentiator today.
ak_onprem_note: docs/getting-started/dspm-overview.md documents discovery and classification only. The AccuKnox row is Coming soon, so on-prem availability cannot be confirmed.

pc_new: No data asset exposure checks. Compute Edition ships the CWPP module only
quote: Prisma Cloud Compute Edition is a self-hosted offering that’s deployed and managed by you. It includes the Cloud Workload Protection Platform (CWPP) module only.
notes: Compute has no CSPM or DSPM, so no public bucket or public data asset detection. WAAS path risks flag API endpoints reachable from the internet, which covers web endpoints and not data stores.
ak_onprem_note: docs/use-cases/cdr.md reads CloudTrail and cloud audit logs, so it applies to the cloud estate. An air-gapped control plane has no cloud log source, and no on-prem page describes CDR.

pc_new: No data policy controls. Compute Edition ships the CWPP module only
quote: Prisma Cloud Compute Edition is a self-hosted offering that’s deployed and managed by you. It includes the Cloud Workload Protection Platform (CWPP) module only.
notes: Compute has no data security policies. WAAS log scrubbing and the runtime log scrubbing rules redact values in logs, which is not a data policy control. The AccuKnox cell for this row is Coming soon.
ak_onprem_note: docs/getting-started/dspm-overview.md lists allow lists, detector toggles and a confidence floor only. The AccuKnox row is Coming soon, so on-prem availability cannot be confirmed.

pc_new: Generic container runtime defense with learned models, but no AI-specific sandbox
quote: Runtime defense is the set of features that provide both predictive and threat-based active protection for running containers.
notes: Compute runtime defense learns a per-image allow list across process, network and filesystem sensors, and it works on any container. It has no policy set built for AI model or agent execution. The image analysis sandbox runs images before deployment and is not an AI runtime sandbox.
ak_onprem_note: docs/use-cases/modelarmor.md says the four ModelArmor controls apply to on-premises model servers and local agents, enforced by KubeArmor with eBPF and LSM on the node, so no cloud reach is needed.

pc_new: WAAS alerts or blocks by source country for web apps, with no model access policy
quote: WAAS will apply action of choice (Alert or Prevent) on all other requests not originating from the specified countries.
notes: The Enterprise-era cell cited UEBA anomaly policies, which are not in Compute. In Compute the nearest control is WAAS country-based access control, which can cover a self-hosted model API served over HTTP. It reads the request source IP and does not see cloud API calls to managed model services.
ak_onprem_note: docs/use-cases/cdr.md raises the unapproved-region alert from cloud audit logs, so it fits the cloud estate. An air-gapped control plane has no cloud log source, and no on-prem page describes CDR.
